items.title: Alex Bigard Interview, 1961-02-07
items.q: And when Toots left, they had Walter D. Coo played piano with us. ... Oh, yeah. I worked with him pretty regular.

ctx.x: Remember his name, Dick? Toots. Is that the real bright down? Yeah. Where does he live? Up in Shrewsbury? Somewhere around that way, yeah. Toots Washington. Oh, yeah. That was a fellow, Toots Washington. Yeah. Placed with Andy Anderson. Yeah. Oh, that fellow, Toots. Yeah. That was just a four-piece band there.
Yeah. And when Toots left, they had Walter D. Coo played piano with us. Mm-hmm. To the place closed.
Mm-hmm. Talking about Walter D. Coo, I believe you said you worked with him way back.
That's where you went to play at the Lyric with John. Where did you go after the Brown Derby?

Well, after the Brown Derby, my next job, I think, was at the Cadillac with Rene. Rene had a job over there. Oh, yeah. Yeah, that's right. He got the job over at the Cadillac. Went for Old Man Coochie.
